reconcile.connective: Defenders distinguish two senses of "face": the familiar, direct converse Moses enjoyed, versus God's unveiled essential glory, which no one may see and live.

discrepancy.connective: The skeptic who compiled this contradiction, Steve Wells, presses that the same Exodus 33 affirms both that the LORD spoke to Moses face to face and that no man can see God's face and live, and reads the two as a flat conflict the harmonizing distinction is invented to escape.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013); contradictions list at skepticsannotatedbible.com

excerpts.excerpt_text: If any one objects to this, that it is at variance with the assertion which we shall come to presently, 'Thou canst not see My face,' the answer is a very simple one. Although Jehovah showed Himself to Moses in some peculiar form of manifestation, He never appeared in His own essential glory, but only in such a mode as human weakness could bear.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: K&D, quoting Calvin, explicitly states the 33:11 / 33:20 objection and answers it by distinguishing the form of manifestation Moses saw from God's essential glory. Most directly on-tension excerpt in the set.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament, on Exodus 33:7-23 (1861-75)
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D treat this passage at length, explicitly raising the 33:11 'face to face' / 33:20 'thou canst not see My face' objection and resolving it by distinguishing the manifested form Moses saw from God's unveiled essential glory.

link.title: GotQuestions: If Moses met face to face with God, why was he not allowed to see God's face?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment of the exact Exodus 33:11 vs 33:20 tension; argues 'face to face' is idiomatic for intimate converse while 'face' in vv. 20-23 denotes God's full glory.
